The Anatomy of a Crisis
Step 1: Innovation & Expansion
Extensive use of machinery and
division of labor leads to the limitless
expansion of production.
Step 2: The Epidemic
The absurdity of Over-Production
Society suddenly finds itself put back
into a state of momentary barbarism.
Step 5: The Inevitable
Consequence
Paving the way for more extensive and
more destructive crises, while
diminishing the means to prevent them.
Step 3: The Crash
Commercial crisis. Destruction of
existing products and previously
created productive forces.
Step 4: The Bourgeois Solution
Enforced destruction of productive
forces + Conquest of new markets.

The Proletariat Condition
The Slave
Condition: Sold once and for all.
• Guarantee of Existence:
Assured an existence, however
miserable, by the master's
interest. Outside of competition.
• Liberation: Abolishes only the
relationship of slavery to
become a proletarian.
The Serf
•Condition: Yields a part of the
product/labor.
• Guarantee of Existence:
Possesses and uses an
instrument of production (a
piece of land). Outside of
competition.
•Liberation: Drives out feudal
lord to become a property
owner.
The Proletarian
•Condition: Must sell himself daily
and hourly. A commodity exposed
to all fluctuations of the market.
• Guarantee of Existence: None.
Dependent entirely on the
demand for labor.
• Liberation: Must abolish private
property and competition in
general.

The Calculus of Wages
The price of a commodity is equal to its cost of production. Therefore, the
price of labor = the minimum means of subsistence required for maintenance and
propagation. As the repulsiveness of work increases, the wage decreases.

The Role of the Communists
What They Are Not
• They do not form a separate party
opposed to other working-class
parties.
• They have no interests separate from
the proletariat as a whole.
• They do not set up sectarian principles
to mold the movement.
What They Are
• Theoretically: They have the advantage
of clearly understanding the line of
march, the conditions, and the ultimate
general results.
•Practically: The most advanced and
resolute section of the working-class
parties.
- Globally: They bring to the front the
common interests of the entire
proletariat, independently of all
nationality.

The Single Sentence: Abolition of Private Property
Personal Property
Hard-won, self-acquired, self-earned
property of the artisan or peasant.
Marxist Verdict: There is no need to abolish
that; the development of industry has to a great
extent already destroyed it.
Bourgeois Private Property
Capital. A collective product set in motion by
the united action of society, capable of
subjugating the labor of others.
Marxist Verdict: This is what must be abolished.
When converted into common property, it only loses
its class character, not its social power.

The Empirical Amendment: Paris, 1871
One thing especially was proved by the Commune... the
working class cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made state
machinery, and wield it for its own purposes. (1872 Preface)
The Trigger
The siege of Paris; the
working class replaces the
army with a National Guard.
The Realization
The centralized state power (standing
army, police, bureaucracy) is an engine
of class despotism. It cannot be
captured; it must be smashed.

- The proletariat organizes
as a class and sweeps
away by force the old
conditions of production.
- By abolishing these
conditions, it abolishes the
conditions for class
antagonism.
- Political power--merely the
organized power of one class
for oppressing another--loses
its political character.
